instruction: Search for 'Spider-Man toys for kids' on Amazon and sort the results by lowest price.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent encountered 'Access Denied' on kohls.com. Navigated to Amazon, searched 'Spider-Man toys for kids', and sorted by 'Price: Low to High'. Task scored 0 because evaluator required kohls.com-specific elements.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome address bar, search products on Amazon, use sort dropdowns, handle blocked sites by navigating elsewhere
metadata.failure_analysis: Kohls.com returned Access Denied. Model adapted by going to Amazon, but evaluator checks kohls.com-specific HTML breadcrumbs and sort selector.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests the exact search+sort capability the model demonstrated on Amazon. Partial credit rewards search (0.5) and sort (0.5) independently.
metadata.explanation: Custom metric checks Amazon search URL for Spider-Man query and price-asc-rank sort parameter, with 0.5 partial credit for each.

scoring_breakdown.search: 0.5 - URL contains Amazon search with Spider-Man query

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the current Chrome URL from the accessibility tree, which is the right state to verify Amazon search and sort.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('search_pattern') and expected.get('sort_pattern') from the rules dict.
Search pattern regex 'amazon\.com/s.*[?&]k=.*[Ss]pider.?[Mm]an' correctly validates the URL is an Amazon search containing 'Spider-Man' query.
Sort pattern 'price-asc-rank|s=price-asc' correctly matches Amazon's price-ascending sort URL parameter.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 search + 0.5 sort) is logical and well-structured.
Minor gap: search_pattern only verifies 'Spider-Man' is in the query but does not check for 'toys for kids', so an agent searching just 'Spider-Man' would get 0.5 credit for search.
Data flow is correct: URL string from getter -> regex match in metric -> float score returned.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider tightening search_pattern to also verify 'toys' or 'kids' appear in the query parameter, e.g. 'amazon\.com/s.*[?&]k=.*[Ss]pider.?[Mm]an.*(?:toys|kids)' to ensure the full search query is validated.
